header.running_head: Leading the Salaah and Following the Imaam During the Time of Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.text: was critically ill) Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a message to Abu Bakr (RA) to lead the salaah. Abu Bakr (RA) was a soft person so he said to Umar (RA), "You lead the salaah, O Umar!" Umar (RA) however said, "You are more worthy of the privilege." Abu Bakr (RA) then led the salaah during those days.

A narration of Bukhaari also quoted in the chapter states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in salaah," Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed. One of Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives remarked, "Abu Bakr is a soft man who will be unable lead the salaah when he stands in your place." Rasulullaah ﷺ however repeated the instruction, but again met with the same response. When this happened a third time, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "You women are just like the women around Yusuf (AS). Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in salaah."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zam'ah (RA) reports, "A few Muslims and I happened to be with Rasulullaah ﷺ when his illness had become critical. When Bilaal (RA) called out the Adhaan, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Appoint someone to lead the salaah.' I left and found Umar (RA) amongst the people. Abu Bakr (RA) was not there. I therefore told Umar (RA) to lead the salaah. Umar (RA) then stood up and when he said 'Allaahu Akbar' Rasulullaah ﷺ heard his voice because his voice was very loud. Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked, 'Then where is Abu Bakr? Neither Allaah nor the Muslims can accept this! Neither Allaah nor the Muslims can accept this!' Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for Abu Bakr (RA) and when he arrived, Umar (RA) had already completed the salaah. Abu Bakr (RA) then lead the people in salaah. Umar (RA) then said to me, 'O dear! What have you done, O Ibn Zam'ah? I swear by Allaah that when you told me to lead the salaah, I thought that it was an instruction from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Had I known better, I would have never led the salaah.' I explained, 'By Allaah! Rasulullaah ﷺ certainly did not instruct me to appoint you but when I did not see Abu Bakr (RA) and only saw you, I regarded you as being most worthy of leading the salaah.'" [^1]

Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ heard Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s voice, he came out and with his head out of the room, he said angrily, "No! No! None but the son of Abu Quhaafah (i.e. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)) should lead the salaah." [^2]

In the chapter discussing how the Sahabah (RA) elected Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) to the post of Khilaafah[^3], a narration has passed in which Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) said, "I am not likely to step head of a person whom Rasulullaah ﷺ had commanded to lead us in salaah and who then led us in salaah until Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away."
Ahmad and Abu Dawood, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.232). Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.641) has reported a similar narration.
